\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}
Decide \AtlasInlineMath{D(A)=\mathbf1\{\operatorname{rank}(A)\ge r+1\}}.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}
The quantity \AtlasInlineMath{A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}} is arbitrary; assume \AtlasInlineMath{d\ge1} and integer threshold \AtlasInlineMath{0\le r<d}.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}
The quantity \AtlasInlineMath{d,r} is public and \AtlasInlineMath{A} hidden. Any \AtlasInlineMath{v\in\mathbb{R}^d} returns exact \AtlasInlineMath{Av}; no transpose channel is available.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}
Return the one-bit decision \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat{D}\in\{0,1\}}; no rank value, witness vector, or certificate is required.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}
The base loss is \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbf1\{\widehat{D}\ne D(A)\}}, and classification must be correct with probability at least \AtlasInlineMath{2/3}.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}
Count right products with single vectors only: \AtlasInlineMath{N=N_{\mathrm r}}. A block of width \AtlasInlineMath{q} costs \AtlasInlineMath{q} calls.

The budget bounds calls for every fixed input and every private seed. Reading public inputs, exact real arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are free. One call applies the interface to one vector.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}
Algorithms may use private randomness and choose query vectors adaptively from the declared domain using all previous responses. Queries and outputs may be arbitrary measurable functions of the transcript; no Krylov or linear-span restriction applies. Exact internal arithmetic, storage, and communication are free in this oracle model. A block query is charged by its number of columns.

The algorithm is selected using only public inputs. For every admissible input fixed before its private seed is generated, the success event has probability at least \AtlasInlineMath{2/3} over that private randomness.

\textbf{Budget convention.} A fixed worst-case budget respected for every input and private seed.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{4. Bounds and supporting evidence}
The following conditions apply to every bound in this profile, in addition to each bound's stated region and algorithm scope.

\textbf{Oracle mapping.} Only exact Av for arbitrary real d-vectors is available, with randomized adaptive queries allowed. Each vector costs one N\_right call; if G has q columns, AG costs q calls.

\textbf{Guarantee mapping.} Correctness probability is at least 2/3 for every fixed real matrix. Gaussian tests achieve probability one per fixed input; the lower bound is still evaluated over the full randomized algorithm class allowed by the specification.

\textbf{Output mapping.} Return low\_rank when rank(A) $\le$ r and high\_rank when rank(A) $\ge$ r + 1. There is no numerical-rank tolerance band.

\textbf{Resource mapping.} Count only right multiplication by a single vector, \AtlasInlineMath{N=N_{\mathrm r}}. A block product of width \AtlasInlineMath{q} costs \AtlasInlineMath{q} calls. The worst-case cap holds for every input and random seed; it is not an expected call count. Reading public inputs and exact internal arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are uncharged. This budget does not certify running time or bit complexity.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{5. Local arguments}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{A1 - Independent Gaussian block queries determine the queried column-space rank almost surely.}
\textbf{Scope.} All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.

Draw a d by (r+1) matrix G with independent standard Gaussian entries and query its columns. For each fixed A, rank(AG)=min\{rank(A),r+1\} almost surely: after an SVD of A, the relevant Gaussian block has maximal possible rank almost surely. Thus rank(AG)<=r exactly when rank(A)<=r. The test uses r+1 queries and is almost surely correct for every fixed input.
